questions.question: What is code-switching?
options: Alternating between two or more languages or varieties within a conversation
Translating a book into another language
Inventing a secret language
Writing computer code
questions.explanation: Code-switching is when multilingual speakers alternate between languages or varieties within a conversation or even a single utterance.

questions.question: What social function can code-switching serve?
options: Signalling solidarity and group identity by switching to a shared minority language
Proving the speaker cannot master either language
Making speech impossible to understand
Avoiding all communication
questions.explanation: Switching to a shared in-group language signals belonging and solidarity - for example, Norwegian-Pakistani teenagers mixing languages with friends.

questions.question: How does translanguaging differ from code-switching?
options: Translanguaging views a speaker's languages as one integrated repertoire rather than separate systems being switched between
Translanguaging applies only to writing
They describe exactly the same theory
Translanguaging requires exactly two languages
questions.explanation: While code-switching describes alternating between distinct languages, translanguaging sees multilinguals as flexibly drawing on one unified linguistic repertoire.

questions.question: What is a benefit of translanguaging in education?
options: Students can use their full linguistic repertoire to understand and learn content
It forces students to forget their first language
It eliminates the need for teachers
It only benefits monolingual students
questions.explanation: Allowing students to draw on all their languages supports comprehension, participation, and deeper learning of content.

questions.question: Is code-switching a sign of poor language skills?
options: No - it requires competence in multiple languages and is often used skilfully for social purposes
Yes - it always shows confusion
Yes - monolinguals communicate better
No - because it happens only by accident
questions.explanation: Research shows code-switching is rule-governed and strategic; it demonstrates command of multiple systems, not deficiency.
